WHAT_HAPPENED: the container rolled back to a snapshot from the FDOT01 C2 era (82f6c84) and then did so a second time, erasing even the recovery notes written between the two. Every mission from FMRCT01 onward, TLMR01 included, was lost from the container together with the C3 raw commitment and all 512 archives.

WHAT_WAS_LOST_AND_RECOVERED.C3_commit: LOST — rebuilt from the archives, not recovered

SOURCES.gives: TLMR01/code and TLMR01/out exactly as C1 and C2 froze them
the C1 and C2 commit objects — could not be unbundled, see below
the three FMRCT01 modules the snapshot lacked
all 512 archives, every tar hash re-verified on the device against the container's pre-rollback manifest

DETERMINISTIC_REPLAY_WAS_NOT_NEEDED.why: the sixteen worlds of TLMR01_RAW_LAW_C_b15 were feared lost because the bridge fell before they reached the disk. They were not: the delivery identifiers survived the rollback, the package was written to the device on reconnection, and its tar hash d0de42ec... matches the hash the container computed before the rollback, member for member. No seed was replayed and none needed to be.

ANCESTRY_LIMITATION.WHAT_COULD_NOT_BE_DONE: the git ancestry from the FDOT01 C2 snapshot up to the FOTSEA01 tip 9f4c70ceeb05b0b8a1f27c4cfc855e125f921ce9 could not be re-imported. Every increment on that path is a THIN bundle, the chain's first link needs objects the snapshot does not hold, and the two bundles that would close it are 183 MB and 674 MB — the staging bridge failed at 4 MB during this window, so neither could be brought across.
ANCESTRY_LIMITATION.WHAT_IS_TRUE_INSTEAD: the CONTENT of C1 and C2 is restored and byte-verified: all 39 modules of the frozen methods closure and all 17 frozen artefacts hash-match, and the master freeze hash and the complete pre-run methods hash both reproduce exactly.
ANCESTRY_LIMITATION.HOW_IT_IS_HANDLED: the restored work is committed on a branch descended from the surviving inherited history, and this record states plainly that C1 and C2 are content-restored and not object-restored. The claim that the frozen state was preserved rests on the hashes, which are checkable, and not on the commit graph, which is not.
